card.name: Lezginka
card.tagline: The Caucasus — Dagestan, Chechnya, Georgia, Azerbaijan. The fast warrior dance that crosses borders.
card.profile: The Lezginka (Russian: Лезгинка) is a folk dance common throughout the North Caucasus. It is named after the Lezgin people. It uses a fast 68 rhythm, and can be either a solo male or a pair dance. According to Encyclopædia Britannica: Lezginka, also spelled Lezghinka, folk dance originating among the Lezgin people of the North Caucasus. It is a male solo dance (often with a sword) and also a couple dance. The man, imitating the eagle, falls to his knees, leaps up, and dances with concise steps and strong, sharp arm and body movements.
card.insight: The dance has also been adapted into classical music in Aram Khachaturian's 1942 ballet Gayane.

Moving shoulders, neck, and head instead of isolating the upper body
Moving arms too fast or bouncing around
lessons.teacher_style: The instructor provides calm, step-by-step guidance, focusing heavily on upper body posture and distinct arm versus leg rhythms. She breaks down movements verbally while demonstrating slowly before applying them to music.
lessons.distinctive_method: Emphasizing the isolation and contrasting speeds between fast leg movements and soft, slow hand movements.
what_works: Isolating upper body and leg instruction before combining them
Showing what not to do contrasted with correct posture
what_hinders: Detailed verbal explanations can sometimes become repetitive
